- If sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- If sentiment turns positive (avg > 0.1) after a recent dip, model often overshoots; cap upward revisions at +3% of recent 7-day mean.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment spikes (e.g., +0.3+), leading to premature price peaks; apply 1–2 day lag correction for spikes > +0.25.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to align with true mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates late-period prices (last 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% on final 5–7 forecast points.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., -0.4 → +0.3 → -0.4), model misreads momentum; adjust forecast to reflect mean reversion toward 14-day moving average.
